notes_list.title: Causes of 1857 Revolt
notes_list.basic_overview: Immediate cause: greased cartridges controversy. Deeper causes: annexation policies (Doctrine of Lapse), economic exploitation, and social/religious interference by the British.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Key leaders: Bahadur Shah Zafar (Delhi), Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Nana Saheb (Kanpur), Tantia Tope. Suppressed by 1858; led to end of East India Company rule (Government of India Act 1858).

notes_list.title: Non-Cooperation Movement
notes_list.basic_overview: Launched by Gandhi in 1920 in response to Jallianwala Bagh massacre and Khilafat issue. Involved boycott of foreign goods, schools, courts and titles.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Called off after Chauri Chaura incident (Feb 1922) where a mob killed policemen, leading Gandhi to withdraw the movement citing violence.

notes_list.title: Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856)
notes_list.basic_overview: Known for the Doctrine of Lapse, expansion of railways and telegraph, and annexation of Awadh (1856) — a major trigger for the 1857 revolt.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Major achievements/reforms: (1) Doctrine of Lapse — annexed Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Jhansi, Nagpur, Awadh. (2) First railway line (Bombay-Thane, 1853) and telegraph line laid. (3) Public Works Department established. (4) Wood's Despatch (1854) — framework for modern English education. (5) Widow Remarriage Act groundwork; postal reforms (uniform postage).
